$comment: Central awareness of the datasets these viewers draw, and of the decisions taken
between a published source and the thing on screen.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Two viewers in this family independently built a file called
glaciations.json from the same underlying compilation, with different schemas, and
neither knew about the other. Nothing was wrong with either -- but a third viewer
would have built a third, and by then 'what does this family say about glaciation'
would have had no answer. This file is that answer.
WHAT IT IS NOT. It is not a canon. These pages are built on the position that several
defensible reconstructions exist and a reader should be able to move between them;
the same applies to every other dataset. So where genuine alternatives exist they are
all listed, none is marked correct, and a viewer is expected to offer the choice
rather than quietly pick one. Inconsistency between viewers is acceptable. Undeclared
inconsistency is not.
THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST is `derivation_choices`. A source publishes something; a
viewer draws something; between the two sit decisions -- a smoothing window, a gap
bridge, a latitude band, a time step. Those are invisible in the rendered page and
invisible in the data file, and they are exactly what these viewers exist to surface.
Anything in `derivation_choices` is OURS, not the source's, and should be marked that
way wherever it reaches a UI.
RELATIONSHIPS between entries under one concept:
variant   - competing estimates of the SAME quantity over the SAME range. A knob.
component - different quantities, or the same one over a DIFFERENT range, composed
into one display. Not a choice: a join, whose seams must be declared.
reduction - the same data processed into a different shape, with the processing
parameters recorded in derivation_choices.
`covers_ma` is [oldest, youngest]. Outside it the answer is NO DATA, which is not the
same as zero and must never be drawn as though it were.

glacial_extent.quantity: angular distance from the pole reached by ice, degrees
glacial_extent.note: The margin latitude is 90 minus this.

entries.source: Macdonald, F.A., Swanson-Hysell, N.L., Park, Y., Lisiecki, L. & Jagoutz, O. (2019), Science 364, 181-184
provenance: tectonic-co2 reads it from the authors' own code_output/ice_LIP_suture_lengths.csv
lips reads it from Ice_Extent.csv in Park et al. (2020)'s repository, their digitisation of the same figure
entries.verified: The two paths were compared at all 105 overlapping ages and agree exactly. They are not variants; they are the same numbers by two routes.

entries.quantity: contiguous glaciated intervals with a peak extent each
entries.source: as macdonald2019, reduced to discrete intervals by this project

bridge_myr.what: Gaps in the continuous record shorter than this are bridged, merging what would otherwise be two glaciations into one.
bridge_myr.effect: Changes how many glaciations the record contains. Not a published parameter.

cryogenian_glaciation.quantity: dated glaciation intervals, each boundary a bracket between two dated horizons
cryogenian_glaciation.note: A different quantity from glacial_extent, over a range that compilation does not reach. Composed with it, never substituted for it. THE SEAM: 579.88-525 Ma is covered by neither and is NO DATA.

entries.source: Hoffman, P.F. et al. (2017), Science Advances 3(11), e1600983, Table 1; Gaskiers from Pu, J.P. et al. (2016), Geology 44(11), 955-958

known_alternatives.status: not a variant -- do not build as one
known_alternatives.source: Rooney, A.D., Strauss, J.V., Brandon, A.D. & Macdonald, F.A. (2015), Geology 43, 459-462
known_alternatives.why: It reads as a rival chronology (Sturtian 717-660 Ma, Marinoan termination 635 Ma) but it is not one: Hoffman et al. (2017) Table 1 cites Rooney's individual Re-Os dates among its own constraints -- 662.4 +/- 3.9 Ma for Laurentia, 659.0 +/- 4.5 for Tuva-Mongolia, >632.3 +/- 5.9 for the basal Sheepbed. Rooney is an INPUT to the entry above, not an alternative to it. Offering both as a knob would invent a disagreement that does not exist.
known_alternatives.a_real_variant_would_be: A compilation drawing on a different body of geochronology, or one weighting the same constraints differently -- e.g. resolving the Sturtian termination toward Laurentia's 662.4 Ma rather than Hoffman's synthesised 659.3-658.5 Ma window. None is currently on disk.

plate_reconstruction.quantity: rotations, and the polygons they move
plate_reconstruction.note: The clearest case of genuine variants in this family, and the one the other concepts should be modelled on: several defensible models, all offered, none marked correct.

entries.source: Merdith, A.S. et al. (2021), Earth-Science Reviews 214, 103477

anchor_plate.effect: Its 001-relative-to-000 sequence is identity, so 0 and 1 agree here.

entries.source: Torsvik, T.H. & Cocks, L.R.M. (2017), Earth History and Palaeogeography, Cambridge University Press

anchor_plate.effect: Plate 001 is the spin axis in this model; anchoring on 000 moves paleolatitude by up to ~9 degrees.

entries.source: Torsvik & Cocks 2017 + Swanson-Hysell & Macdonald + Domeier (2018), as distributed in Macdonald et al.'s Arc_Continent_Analysis repository
entries.note: The SAME NAMED MODEL as TorsvikCocks2017 from a different rotation file. At 445 Ma they place Laurentia 13 degrees apart in latitude, which roughly halves tropical suture length at the Hirnantian. Kept as separate entries deliberately: that disagreement is the point, not a defect to reconcile.

suture_compilation.quantity: ophiolite-bearing suture geometry with magmatic, metamorphic and exhumation age intervals

entries.note: 115 sutures. Carries three plate-ID columns of its own -- PLATEID1 (Merdith2021), PLATEID_M (Matthews2016), PLATEID_CE (CEED). This project assigns no plate IDs.

activity_definition.whose: source tabulates all four; the published curve used one

band_edge.whose: hard is published; the taper is OURS
band_edge.effect: Whether a suture crossing the edge counts fully or partly.

time_step_myr.effect: Matches the source's own 5 Myr output rather than implying finer precision.

lip_compilation.quantity: large igneous province extents and areas through time

entries.source: Ernst, R.E. & Youbi, N. (2017) present-day extents, edited by Park et al. (2020), AGU Geophysical Monograph 255, doi:10.1002/9781119507444

continental_arc_length.quantity: continental arc length through time, km

entries.source: Cao, W., Zahirovic, S., Flament, N., Williams, S., Golonka, J. & Muller, R.D. (2017), Biogeosciences 14, 5425-5439
entries.note: Shipped inside tectonic-co2/data/macdonald2019.json as the continental_arc_Cao2017 column, verbatim. Binned at 10 Myr by the source.
